opportunities.title: The Pope's Prayer App Leaked 700K Souls' Data — Even the Vatican Isn't Patch-Immune
opportunities.why_now: A widely-covered breach of a religious institution's app is a rare, highly shareable story that dropped simultaneously on The Register and Dark Reading in the last 24 hours.
opportunities.angle: Wry breach-digest writeup: what leaked (PII of 700K+ users), how a supposedly trusted app failed basic security hygiene, and the broader lesson that no org is too sacred to skip patch cadence.

opportunities.title: Oracle Just Shipped 1,449 Patches — And That's the New Normal
opportunities.why_now: A quarterly patch dump of nearly 1,500 fixes is a stark, quantifiable illustration of unsustainable patch cadence that fits the channel's core beat perfectly.
opportunities.angle: Data-driven patch-cadence piece: break down patch count trend over recent quarters, highlight critical CVEs buried in the pile, and ask if 'patch everything' is even achievable anymore.

opportunities.title: Cl0p's New Playground: Unauthenticated RCE in PTC Windchill and FlexPLM Under Active Attack

opportunities.angle: Threat-actor spotlight: who Cl0p is, why internet-exposed PLM/PDM systems are a juicy target, and immediate mitigation steps for orgs running Windchill/FlexPLM.

opportunities.title: Russia's Zimbra Zero-Day Has Been Quietly Hitting US and Ukraine for Months
opportunities.why_now: A nation-state-linked zero-day actively exploited against US and Ukrainian targets is exactly the inevitable-breach material this channel thrives on, and it's freshly reported.
opportunities.angle: Threat-actor + CVE deep dive: timeline of exploitation, Zimbra's patch status, and what defenders should watch for in mail-server logs.

opportunities.title: Fastjson Has an RCE Being Exploited in the Wild — And There's No Patch
opportunities.why_now: Active in-the-wild exploitation of a legacy library with zero available patch is a rare 'no fix exists' emergency that demands immediate attention from dev/ops teams.
opportunities.angle: Urgent advisory-style post: explain the vuln, who's exploiting it, why Fastjson 1.x can't easily be patched, and workaround/mitigation options (WAF rules, dependency removal).
